summary.name: Usagebar
summary.one_liner: A free, open source macOS menu bar app that shows usage limits (5-hour window, weekly cap, reset times) for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code, z.ai and Grok Build.
use_cases: Check Claude Code 5-hour and weekly limits from the Mac menu bar
Monitor Codex CLI rate limits and reset times
Track Cursor and Grok Bot shared weekly allowance
Watch usage across several AI coding CLIs in one place
Install a menu bar usage indicator via Homebrew
summary.what_it_does: Usagebar is a macOS menu bar app that reads the local sign-in data already created by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code, z.ai and Grok Build. It displays the 5-hour rolling window and weekly usage for each provider, plus when limits reset. Right-clicking the menu bar item opens a panel with a meter for each provider's limits. It refreshes every 2 minutes and can show one provider, rotate between them, or follow the AI app in use. Installation is via a single Homebrew cask command, with an install script as a fallback.
notable: Reads existing CLI sign-in stores (Keychain, ~/.codex/auth.json, etc.) so no extra setup is needed
Credentials stay local; no telemetry, analytics, or hosted sync
Free and open source under the MIT license
caveats: Currently macOS only; a Windows and Linux version is described as in development
Each provider must already be signed in on the Mac (e.g. claude login, codex login, kimi login)
z.ai requires a Z_AI_API_KEY or its config file
